headline: Elche cannot score, and Rayo cannot finish
summary: Elche have scored 0 goals in their last two matches and average 0.86 expected goals a game, which is why they arrive at Vallecas as clear outsiders. Rayo made 2.26 expected goals at Getafe on Monday and still only drew: the chances come, the goals do not. Rayo's right-back Ratiu is doubtful after 540 minutes this season, though Ciss's yellow-card appeal succeeded, Spanish media report. Across ten bookmakers, margin removed, Rayo are 54% favourites, rated about two-thirds of a goal better. The market expects 2.6 goals in total: a home win, but not a heavy one.
read: Rayo Vallecano are clear home favourites at 54.0% against an Elche side with one win in nine that sits in the relegation zone. The market rates Rayo about two-thirds of a goal the better team and leans slightly to over 2.5 goals, with Vallecas under partial closure and both squads close to full strength.

facts.fact: Rayo Vallecano are 54.0% to win at home, more than double Elche's 21.3%.
facts.meaning: The market makes a home win more likely than not, with Elche given roughly a one-in-five chance at Vallecas.

facts.fact: Elche have won once in nine La Liga games — W1 D4 L4 — and sit in the relegation zone.
facts.meaning: They arrive needing a result, having drawn four of their nine matches.

facts.fact: Rayo serve a partial stadium closure and a €6,000 fine for this match, with only 143 tickets made available to Elche fans.
facts.meaning: A reduced, tense Vallecas: the home backing is thinner and the mood around the club is sour, with supporters' groups still protesting against president Martín Presa.

facts.fact: The market's fair handicap line is Rayo -0.67, played on a -0.75 line.
facts.meaning: Rayo are rated about two-thirds of a goal the better team — closer to a one-goal win than to a draw.

facts.fact: Rayo drew 1-1 at Getafe on Monday, generating 2.26 xG to Getafe's 0.61.
facts.meaning: They are creating far more than they concede but scoring once; chance creation is strong, finishing is not.
The market's fair goal total is 2.6 — a slight lean to over, not a strong one.

facts.fact: Rayo's appeal over Pathé Ciss's fifth yellow card succeeded — the Disciplinary Committee cleared him to face Elche.
facts.meaning: Rayo keep an ever-present defender with 765 minutes in nine appearances this season, rather than patching the back line.

facts.fact: Elche trained on Wednesday with only one absentee: Marc Aguado, out with an ankle injury.
facts.meaning: Anselmi has virtually a full squad; Aguado's 375 minutes and one goal from midfield is the only hole to fill.

sources.fact: Rayo Vallecano will serve a partial stadium closure and a €6,000 fine for the match against Elche, with only 143 tickets available to Elche fans.
Rayo Vallecano supporters' groups reject the punishment and maintain their protests against club president Martín Presa.
Pathé Ciss will be available to play against Elche after the Disciplinary Committee overturned his fifth yellow card of the season following a successful Rayo appeal.
Rayo Vallecano players did not train at the Ciudad Deportiva 72 hours before the Elche match, according to Mundo Deportivo.
Rayo Vallecano drew 1-1 at Getafe in their previous La Liga match, having taken the lead and playing over an hour with a numerical advantage for Getafe.

Spain's anti-violence commission has proposed bans and fines for 12 Rayo Vallecano supporters who threw paper airplanes and other objects onto the pitch, forcing the suspension of the La Liga match against Athletic Bilbao.
Elche goalkeeper Matías Dituro said the team is "on the right track" and "growing", noting they have taken five points from the last three games but "need to get a win" against Rayo Vallecano.
Dituro credited Elche's growth to the work of coach Anselmi and urged focus on the match at Vallecas.
